result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_valid_tree_degree_sequence()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Check whether a degree sequence is the degree sequence of some tree. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_valid_tree_degree_sequence()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Check whether a degree sequence is the degree sequence of some tree. title: >- [Graph.is_valid_tree_degree_sequence()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Check whether a degree sequence is the degree sequence of some tree. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check whether a degree sequence is the degree sequence of some tree. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16073-L16128){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_valid_tree_degree_sequence(degree_sequence) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is valid tree degree sequence](/assets/graphs/is-valid-tree-degree-sequence.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Each side draws a graph with the degree sequence passed in, its degrees as badges. Left: [3, 1, 1, 1] has every degree positive and sums to 6 = 2(n - 1) for n = 4 nodes, so it is realized by a tree, the star, and the method returns True. Right: [2, 2, 2, 2] sums to 8, more than the 6 a tree on four nodes has; its graphs need an extra edge, closing a cycle (the edge in the accent color), so the method returns False." width="100%"} A list of degrees belongs to a tree exactly when two conditions hold: the degrees sum to `2 * (n - 1)`, since a tree on `n` nodes has `n - 1` edges and each edge adds 2 to the sum, and every degree is positive, since a tree with more than one node has no isolated nodes. The single-node tree has sequence `[0]`. When both hold, a tree can always be built (for instance by repeatedly joining a leaf to a node that still needs edges), so no further test is needed. This is NetworkX's `is_valid_tree_degree_sequence()`, which returns the reason for a failure alongside the verdict; here the result is a plain boolean. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [degree_sequence]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The degrees, in any order. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if some tree has these degrees. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The empty sequence is not a tree degree sequence (a tree has at least one node). ## Examples {.doc-examples} A star on four nodes and a path on four nodes pass; a cycle's degrees fail the sum condition and a sequence with a zero fails the positivity condition: ::: {#2d9ad09a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec [ ec.Graph.is_valid_tree_degree_sequence(seq) for seq in ([3, 1, 1, 1], [1, 2, 2, 1], [2, 2, 2, 2], [2, 2, 0, 1, 1]) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [True, True, False, False] ``` ::: ::: Every tree's degrees pass: ::: {#97f60a63 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree = ec.Graph().add_random_labeled_tree(12, seed=3) degrees = [tree.get_degree(n) for n in tree.get_node_ids()] degrees, ec.Graph.is_valid_tree_degree_sequence(degrees) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ([1, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 2], True) ``` ::: :::
